concepts.name: Legal Basis and Establishment of State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs)
key_dimensions: Section 22 of Biological Diversity Act, 2002 as the statutory basis for SBB formation
Mandatory vs. discretionary nature of SBB establishment by state governments
Relationship between Central Government direction and State autonomy in constituting SBBs
Comparison with NBA (National Biodiversity Authority) establishment under Section 8 — same Act, different tiers

concepts.name: Composition and Membership of State Biodiversity Boards
key_dimensions: Chairperson qualification criteria — ex-officio or eminent person, appointment by State Government
Number of ex-officio members vs. non-official members and prescribed ratio
Representation of women and marginalized communities — statutory requirement or gap
Comparison with NBA composition: Secretary-level vs. state-level appointments — UPSC trap on hierarchy

concepts.name: Regulatory Role of SBBs — Prior Intimation vs. Prior Approval
key_dimensions: Section 7 of BD Act: Indian entities (citizens/companies) need only to 'intimate' SBB, not seek approval — critical distinction
Contrast with Section 3 (foreign entities requiring NBA approval) — jurisdictional boundary trap
What constitutes 'access to biological resources' triggering Section 7 obligation
Consequences of non-intimation — penalties under Section 55 of BD Act

concepts.name: SBB Exemptions — Local Communities and Vaids/Hakims
key_dimensions: Section 7 proviso: exemption for local communities, growers, cultivators for personal use
Exemption for practitioners of indigenous medicine (Vaids, Hakims) — scope and limits
UPSC trap: exemption applies to SBB jurisdiction, NOT to NBA — different exemption regimes
Policy tension between protecting traditional knowledge and regulating commercial exploitation

concepts.name: SBB's Power to Notify Biodiversity Heritage Sites (BHS)
key_dimensions: Section 37 of BD Act: State Government notifies BHS in consultation with local bodies — SBB's advisory role
Distinction between BHS (state-level, Section 37) and Biological Diversity Act's other conservation tools
Management responsibility after notification — State Government vs. local bodies vs. SBB
Comparison with Protected Areas under Wildlife Protection Act — overlap and UPSC confusion point

concepts.name: SBB's Relationship with Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)
key_dimensions: Section 41: BMCs established at local body level — SBB's supervisory and guiding role over BMCs
People's Biodiversity Register (PBR) preparation — BMC's primary role, SBB's oversight function
Gram Panchayat vs. Urban Local Body — both mandated to constitute BMCs under SBB guidance
UPSC trap: BMCs are NOT under NBA directly — SBB is the intermediary tier in the three-tier structure

concepts.name: Three-Tier Biodiversity Governance Structure — SBB's Position
key_dimensions: NBA (national) → SBB (state) → BMC (local) — hierarchical roles and non-overlapping jurisdictions
Difference in subject-matter jurisdiction: foreign access (NBA), Indian commercial use (SBB), local documentation (BMC)
Fund flow: NBA receives ABS proceeds → shares with SBBs → SBBs to BMCs — financial linkage
UPSC trap: SBBs do NOT 'control' NBA; they operate under BD Act independently with state government oversight

concepts.name: Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) — SBB's Facilitation Role
key_dimensions: SBB's role in determining benefit-sharing conditions when Indian companies access state biological resources
Nagoya Protocol (2010) ratified by India in 2012 — how it strengthens SBB's ABS mandate
Distinction: NBA finalizes ABS agreements with foreign entities; SBB oversees ABS for domestic commercial use
State Biodiversity Fund (Section 32) — SBB manages it; sources include fees, grants, ABS proceeds

concepts.name: State Biodiversity Fund — Constitution, Management, and Utilization
key_dimensions: Section 32 of BD Act: establishment of State Biodiversity Fund credited to Consolidated Fund of State or separate fund — nuance
Permissible uses: conservation of biodiversity, socio-economic development of local communities
SBB's fiduciary role vs. NBA's role in National Biodiversity Fund — parallel but distinct structures
Audit and accountability mechanisms — CAG oversight applicability

concepts.name: SBB's Advisory Role to State Government
key_dimensions: Section 23(c): SBBs advise state governments on biodiversity conservation matters including EIA processes
Role in State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCC) — biodiversity component advisory function
SBB consultation in land-use change decisions affecting biological diversity — non-binding nature: a governance gap
Comparison with NBA's advisory role to Central Government — symmetrical but weaker enforcement at state level

concepts.name: People's Biodiversity Register (PBR) — SBB's Oversight Function
key_dimensions: PBR documents local biological resources, knowledge, and practices — prepared by BMCs under SBB guidance
Legal status of PBR: evidentiary value in IPR disputes and ABS negotiations
SBB's role in standardizing PBR format, training BMC members, and periodic review
UPSC trap: PBR is NOT the same as National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) — different instruments, different levels

concepts.name: SBB's Role in Checking Biopiracy
key_dimensions: Monitoring unauthorized access to biological resources within state territory — enforcement gap in practice
Interface with Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) — TKDL under CSIR, not SBB, but complementary
SBB's power to approach courts for injunction against biopiracy (Section 56 — civil remedies)
Case studies: Turmeric, Neem, Basmati — lessons for SBB's preventive documentation role

concepts.name: Overlap and Jurisdictional Conflicts Between SBB and Other State Bodies
key_dimensions: SBB vs. State Forest Department — forest produce access regulation: overlapping mandates on NTFPs
SBB vs. State Pollution Control Board — no formal coordination mechanism despite shared environmental mandate
SBB vs. State Wildlife Board — BHS notification vs. Wildlife Sanctuary declaration: dual notification possibility
UPSC trap: SBB has no authority over Scheduled Tribes' traditional use — Forest Rights Act, 2006 operates independently

concepts.name: Penalties and Enforcement Powers of SBBs
key_dimensions: Section 55: penalties for contravening Section 7 (failure to intimate SBB) — imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both
SBB's limited direct enforcement — must approach State Government or courts, lacks independent police powers
Comparison with NBA enforcement powers — symmetrical penalties but NBA has additional power to compound offences
Cognizance of offences: no court shall take cognizance except on complaint by NBA/SBB — Section 61 safeguard

concepts.name: Challenges in SBB Functioning — Implementation Gaps
key_dimensions: Inadequate staffing, funding, and technical capacity — most SBBs non-functional or under-resourced
Low BMC constitution rate across states — SBB's supervisory role remains notional in many states
Lack of awareness among Indian companies about Section 7 intimation requirement — regulatory gap
Parliamentary Standing Committee and CAG reports highlighting SBB dysfunction — governance accountability angle

concepts.name: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 — Impact on SBB's Role
key_dimensions: 2023 Amendment exempts AYUSH practitioners, seed sector, and codified traditional knowledge from BD Act provisions — reduces SBB's regulatory load
Controversy: critics argue amendment weakens ABS regime and reduces SBB's ability to check commercial exploitation
Fast-tracking of research by Indian researchers — SBB's prior intimation requirement relaxed for certain categories
UPSC current affairs angle: 2023 Amendment passed amid protests from biodiversity experts and tribal groups

concepts.name: SBB's Role in Species Conservation vs. Ecosystem Conservation
key_dimensions: BD Act focuses on biological resources broadly — SBB not limited to endangered species unlike WPA's Schedule-based approach
SBB's mandate to conserve agro-biodiversity and landraces — interface with Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
Marine biodiversity jurisdiction — SBBs of coastal states vs. NBA's role in Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ): jurisdictional limit
UPSC trap: SBB jurisdiction ends at territorial waters; beyond that, Central Government/NBA acts

concepts.name: Coordination Between NBA and SBBs — Institutional Linkages
key_dimensions: Section 23(d): SBBs shall take steps to implement guidelines of NBA — subordinate but not hierarchically controlled
Sharing of ABS proceeds: NBA's national fund partially channeled to SBBs for state-level conservation
Joint inspection and monitoring: no formal joint mechanism prescribed in BD Act — implementation gap
Annual report submission: SBBs report to State Legislature; NBA reports to Parliament — parallel accountability tracks

concepts.name: SBBs and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Process
key_dimensions: SBB as a consulted body in EIA for projects affecting biodiversity-rich areas — advisory, not decision-making role
EIA Notification 2006 does not explicitly mandate SBB consultation — gap between BD Act mandate and EIA framework
Biodiversity Impact Assessment (BIA) as an emerging tool — SBB's potential role in mainstreaming it
UPSC angle: conflict between development projects and SBB's advisory objections — non-binding nature as a governance flaw

concepts.name: International Obligations and SBB's Domestic Implementation Role
key_dimensions: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) 1992 — three objectives: conservation, sustainable use, ABS; SBBs operationalize the third at state level
Nagoya Protocol on ABS (2010, in force 2014) — SBBs as domestic checkpoint authorities for compliance
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022) — 30×30 target and SBBs' role in area-based conservation
UPSC trap: India's NBSAP is prepared by MoEFCC/NBA, not SBBs — SBBs implement, not formulate, national strategy
